title: Northern Thai Coconut Curry Noodle Soup with Chicken
summary: A Northern Thai-style coconut curry noodle soup with tender chicken drumsticks, a fragrant homemade chilli-and-herb paste, and a topping of crisp fried noodles.
equipment: large heavy pot (about 5 l) with a lid

ingredients.item: coriander stems, chopped (keep the leaves for serving)
palm sugar or light brown sugar

steps.title: Soak the dried chillies
steps.text: Pour the boiling water over the dried chillies in the small bowl and leave for 10 minutes. The hot water softens their tough skins so they blend into a smooth paste rather than leaving flecks behind. Keep the soaking liquid, as it goes into the paste too.

steps.title: Blend the curry paste
steps.text: Tip the soaked chillies and their liquid into the small food processor with the coriander stems, shallots, turmeric, lemongrass, ginger, garlic, curry powder and lime zest. Blend for about 5 minutes, scraping down the sides often, until completely smooth. A fully smooth paste dissolves evenly into the coconut milk instead of leaving gritty bits in the finished soup.

steps.title: Fry the crisp noodle topping
steps.text: Heat the oil in the medium saucepan to 160°C. Fry 60g of the noodles in batches, flipping once, for 30-60 seconds until golden and crisp, then lift them onto kitchen paper with the slotted spoon. Turn off the heat and leave the oil to cool completely before straining it for another use; the noodles firm up and turn brittle as they cool, which is the texture you're after.

steps.title: Fry the paste
steps.text: Scoop about 60ml of the thick cream from the top of a coconut milk can into the large pot and set it over medium heat for around 10 seconds, just until it melts. Add the paste and stir for 1-2 minutes until deeply fragrant and starting to stick to the base; this brief fry in the coconut fat concentrates the chilli and aromatics. Stir in the remaining coconut milk and the stock, and bring just to a low boil, about 3 minutes.

steps.title: Simmer the chicken
steps.text: Add the drumsticks to the pot, cover and simmer gently for 25-30 minutes, turning once, until the chicken is tender and reaches 74°C near the bone. Gentle simmering keeps the meat moist while the broth slowly takes on flavour from the bone and skin. Once done, stir in the water, fish sauce and sugar, tasting before adding any extra fish sauce since brands vary in saltiness.

steps.title: Cook the remaining noodles
steps.text: While the soup finishes, cook the remaining 240g of noodles in a large pan of unsalted boiling water according to the packet instructions, usually 3-5 minutes, until just tender. Drain well so they don't dilute the broth. They should be soft but still have a little bite.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Divide the noodles among four deep bowls, add two drumsticks to each, and ladle over the hot coconut broth. Finish with the crisp fried noodles, sliced red onion, coriander leaves and lime wedges for squeezing over at the table.

tips: Taste the broth before adding extra fish sauce — pastes and sauces vary a lot in saltiness, so it's easy to overdo it.
Blend the paste until completely smooth; a grainy paste won't melt properly into the coconut milk and can taste gritty in the finished soup.
Keep the crisp noodles separate until the bowls are assembled, so the topping stays crunchy instead of going soft in the hot broth.
safety: Let the frying oil cool completely before straining it; hot oil splashes and scorches if handled too soon.

Frying safety: use a heavy, deep pot no more than half full of oil, with a clip-on thermometer, and dry the food before it goes in. Never leave hot oil unattended. If the oil catches fire, turn off the heat and cover the pot with a metal lid or use a fire extinguisher; never use water.
storage: Cool the soup quickly and refrigerate within 1 hour; use within 3 days. Store the noodles separately from the broth and crisp topping, and reheat the broth and chicken until piping hot (74°C) before combining with freshly cooked noodles. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
